For exact independent k=5 encoding, left-pad item IDs by four, then `unfold(1,5,1)` produces B×L×5 windows. Select valid training positions, flatten windows into the batch dimension, embed with shared SASRec weights, reset positional IDs within each window, apply causal and padding masks, and retain each window’s final state. Define short-prefix positions consistently: fixed right-aligned slots or compact positions starting at zero. PyTorch documents `unfold` as a view; embedding/materialization still costs memory. Process windows in chunks before embedding. With `TransformerEncoder`, padding-mask True means blocked; SDPA boolean-mask True means allowed. Avoid fully masked attention rows for padded queries. [Tensor.unfold](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/2.14/generated/torch.Tensor.unfold.html), [Transformer masks](https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch/blob/main/torch/nn/modules/transformer.py).

Multilayer sliding-window attention is architecturally different: intermediate tokens already contain information from their earlier neighborhoods. With window width five including self, D causal layers can reach back 4D positions, exceeding an independent five-item window. Reset learned absolute positions also makes overlapping items receive different embeddings in different windows, preventing straightforward reuse. This receptive-field expansion is described in [Mistral 7B](https://arxiv.org/abs/2310.06825).

Derived encoder cost for N valid positions, depth D, width d and feedforward width f: independent windows require O(DN[kd²+kdf+k²d]); full-sequence encoding requires O(DB[Ld²+Ldf+L²d]). Small k reduces attention work but repeats projections/feedforward computation. Chunkwise backward bounds saved activations; normalize summed losses by the total valid-position count and step once after all chunks. Four ablations fit only if measured total training, validation, diagnosis and failed-trial GPU time stays within 43,200 seconds—10,800 seconds per ablation on average, including all four categories. Concurrent slots reduce elapsed time, not aggregate GPU seconds.
